validated_results.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort analysis reporting alcohol intake and incident prostate cancer risk with a hazard ratio and confidence interval.

extraction.comparison_type: Alcohol intake tertile 3 vs tertile 1 among individuals with low dietary fiber intake
extraction.population: Adults participating in the Supplémentation en Vitamines et Minéraux Antioxydants study (2771 men for prostate cancer)

sample_size.excerpt: This prospective observational analysis included 3771 women and 2771 men who participated in the Supplémentation en Vitamines et Minéraux Antioxydants study (1994-2007) and completed at least 6 valid 24-h dietary records during the first 2 y of follow-up. After a median follow-up of 12.1 y, 297 incident hormone-dependent cancer cases, including 158 breast and 123 prostate cancers, were diagnosed.

cases.excerpt: After a median follow-up of 12.1 y, 297 incident hormone-dependent cancer cases, including 158 breast and 123 prostate cancers, were diagnosed.

effect_size.excerpt: tertile 1: HR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.10, 2.82; P-trend = 0.002), breast cancer (HR: 2.53; 95% CI: 1.30, 4.95; P-trend = 0.02), and prostate cancer (HR: 1.37; 95% CI: 0.65, 2.89; P-trend = 0.02) risk among individuals with low dietary fiber intake but not among their counterparts with higher dietary fiber intake (P-trend = 0.9, 0.8, and 0.6, respectively). The P-interaction between alcohol and dietary fiber intake was statistically significant for prostate cancer (P = 0.01) but not for overall hormone-dependent (P = 0.2) or breast (P = 0.9) cancer.
